info.title: linq
info.summary: Self-hosted URL shortener and dynamic-link service.
info.description:
Three things share one port: the REST API under `/api`, the Client UI's
static export under `/home`, and the redirect on every other path.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/v1/*` route needs an API key, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-Api-Key: <key>`. A key is the principal:
nobody logs in, and there are no user accounts. A key whose `expires_at` has
passed fails with 401.

**Roles** are ordered `viewer < author < manager < admin`. Each operation
below states the minimum it needs.

**Errors** all share one envelope, documented on the `Error` schema.

**Lists** all share one envelope — `{ data, total, limit, offset }` — where
`total` counts every row matching the filters, not just the page.

---

Written by hand from `apps/server/src/http/`, which stays the source of
truth; the zod schemas in `packages/shared/src/` are what the server
actually validates against, and the constraints here mirror them.

The calling key. There is no user behind it: a key carries its own name and role, and this is what the Client UI gates its menus on.
Ordered by host. Every role may read.

patch.description:
Requires: **admin**. `host` is immutable and is not accepted.

Archiving is refused while any **active** link points at the domain.

409.description: The domain still has active links.

delete.description:
Requires: **admin**. `DELETE` archives; it never destroys. An archived
domain returns an untracked 404 for everything. See `docs/adr/0002`.

409.description: The domain still has active links.

delete.description:
Requires: **admin**. Irreversible, and refused unless the domain is
already archived — archiving and purging are always two deliberate
steps. Refused while **any** link row still points at the domain,
archived ones included.

This is the one operation in linq that loses analytics history: a
domain's visits and rollups go with it.

409.description: Not archived yet, or links still point at it.

get.summary: Grouped visit totals for one domain
get.description:
Every visit on the domain, orphans included.

Unlike the link report this does **not** 404 on an unknown id: an
archived domain still has a history worth reading, and an id that
matches nothing simply reports nothing.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring match, case-insensitive, over slug, name and destination.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated. A link matches when it carries **any** of them.

parameters.name: expiry
parameters.description: Filters on expires_at against the current time. `live` includes links that never expire.

post.description:
Requires: **author**. The caller becomes the owner.

Omit `slug` for a generated one. A custom slug that is taken on that
domain — including by an archived link — is a 409.

409.description: The slug is taken, the domain is archived, or no free slug could be allocated.

get.description: Just the `total` a page from `GET /links` would also carry, for a caller — such as the sidebar's link/archive badges — that never needed the rows or the joins that build them. Takes only `status`; every other list filter is out of scope here.

patch.description:
Requires: **author** for a link you own, **manager** for any link.

`slug` and `domain_id` are immutable, and the body is strict, so sending
either is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field. Changing
`owner_id` additionally needs **admin**, unless you are transferring your
own link.

409.description: The target of `owner_id` is a viewer key, which may not own a link.

delete.description:
Requires: **author** for a link you own, **manager** for any link.

`DELETE` archives; it never destroys. An archived link stops
redirecting — its slug becomes an orphan visit — but keeps its row, its
visits and its reservation on that slug. Reversible by
`PATCH { "status": "active" }`. See `docs/adr/0002`.

Requires: **admin**. Irreversible, and refused unless the link is
already archived.

Its rules go with it. Its visits survive as **orphan visits**, and its
rollups are merged into the orphan scope — history is kept, attribution
is not. Unlike archiving, this **releases the slug** for anyone to claim
on that domain.

409.description: The link is not archived yet.

get.description: In `position` order, which is the order they are evaluated in.

put.description:
Requires: **author** for a link you own, **manager** for any link.

Replaces the whole ordered set in one transaction; the server owns
`position` and assigns it from the array order. Send `[]` to remove
every rule.

200.description: The stored rules, in their new order.

get.summary: Grouped visit totals for one link

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring match, case-insensitive, over the QR code's own name and its link's name and slug.

post.description: Requires: **author** on the target link's owner, **manager** for any link. A QR code is always attached to a link — `link_id` is required — and the link must be active: an archived link's short URL does not resolve, so a code for one would be born dead.

patch.description: Requires: **author** for the owner of the QR code's link, **manager** for any. `link_id` is immutable — re-pointing a QR code at a different link would invalidate every printed copy — and the body is strict, so sending it is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field.

delete.description: Requires: **author** for the owner of the QR code's link, **manager** for any. Hard delete, not archive: a QR code has no slug and no redirect, so archiving one would be ceremony with no consequence. See `docs/adr/0002`'s 2026-09-21 amendment. There is no purge route for QR codes.

get.summary: Grouped visit totals across the instance
get.description:
Optionally narrowed to one domain, or to the orphan slice — the visits
that resolved to no link at all.

Newest first, narrowed by `link_id`, `domain_id` or `orphan`. One route
for every scope, because the only thing that changes between them is a
predicate.

Unlike the reports above, this reads the detail table: a visit row is
the only place a user agent, a query string or an exact instant
survives. Its window is therefore in **instants**, not whole days.

An id that matches nothing reports nothing rather than 404ing — this is
the log with a filter on it, not a view of one link.

get.description: Every role may list keys, but only an admin sees more than `{ id, name }` — the Client UI needs the names to show a link's owner and to offer a transfer target.

post.description: Requires **admin**. The only response that ever carries the plaintext secret.

patch.description: Requires **admin**. Changing the role of the key you are calling with is a 403.

delete.description: Requires **admin**. A real delete, not an archive. Any link the key owned becomes unowned rather than blocking the revoke, so a leaked key is always revocable at once. Revoking the key you are calling with is a 403.

post.description:
Moves every link `id` owns to another key, or to nobody, in one call. The same move `DELETE /keys/{id}` already makes automatically for a revoked key's links — this is for doing it ahead of time, such as before demoting a key that owns links to viewer (which the role change alone would otherwise refuse with a 409).

Requires: **admin** for any key, or the key's own owner (author or higher) reassigning its own.

to.description: The key to move the links to. Null leaves them unassigned.

404.description: The target key (`to`) does not exist.

409.description: The target key is a viewer, which may not own a link.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description:
The path segment after the host. An empty path is the domain root,
which resolves to the fallback URL.

get.description:
The product. Matched last, so every path linq answers itself — `/api`,
`/home`, `/health`, `/robots.txt`, `/favicon.ico` — wins first and can
never be claimed as a slug.

Resolution: the `Host` header selects the domain, the slug selects the
link, then the first rule whose conditions all hold supplies the
destination, falling back to the link's own. With `forward_query` on,
the incoming query is merged over the destination's, incoming winning.

An unknown host, or an archived one, is an **untracked** 404. A live
domain with no matching active link is an **orphan visit**: recorded,
then sent to the domain's `fallback_url`, or 404 if it has none.

`GET` is recorded; `HEAD` is answered identically and never recorded.

302.description:
Always 302, never cached: the destination can change under a live
slug at any time.

404.description: Unknown host, archived domain, or no link and no fallback URL.

head.summary: Resolve a short link without recording a visit

get.description: Disallows `/api` and `/home`. See `/llms.txt` for the catalogue of links a domain has chosen to publish.

Lists links from the requested host that were explicitly opted in with `listed: true` — archived, expired and unlisted links never appear. No key required: this route sits outside `/api/v1` by design. See `docs/adr/0013`.

404.description: The host does not match an active domain.

head.summary: Published link catalogue, without a body

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: Accepted as a fallback for clients that cannot set `Authorization`.

StatsFrom.name: from
StatsFrom.description:
Inclusive first day, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. A whole day, not an
instant: reports are served from a day-grained rollup and a window that
cut a day in half could not be answered from it. See `docs/adr/0007`.

StatsTo.name: to
StatsTo.description: Inclusive last day, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC.

GroupBy.name: group_by
GroupBy.description:
The dimension to bucket on. `day` comes back in chronological order so a
chart can plot it as given; every other dimension is ranked by volume,
busiest first.

Orphan.name: orphan
Orphan.description: Restrict to visits that resolved to no link at all.

StatsBuckets.description:
One bucket per key that had at least one visit. Buckets with no visits
are **absent rather than zero** — only the caller knows which days the
window was meant to cover, so filling the gaps is the caller's job.

ValidationFailed.description: The request failed schema validation. `details` carries the issues.

Forbidden.description: The caller is known but not allowed to do this.

Error.description:
Every error response in linq has this shape. `code` maps one-to-one onto
the status: `validation_failed` 400, `unauthorized` 401, `forbidden` 403,
`not_found` 404, `conflict` 409, `internal` 500.

details.description: Present on `validation_failed`, carrying the zod issues.

Page.description: The envelope every list shares. `total` counts all matching rows, not the page.

ResourceStatus.description: Links and domains are archived, never deleted.

Platform.description: Derived from the user agent; anything unrecognised is `desktop`.

fallback_url.description: Where orphan visits go. Null means 404.

base_path_redirect.description: Where a bare GET / on this host goes. Null falls back to fallback_url.

invalid_short_url_redirect.description: Where a malformed (not just unknown) slug goes. Null falls back to fallback_url.

link_count.description: Every link on the domain, archived included — the count that must reach zero before the domain may be archived or purged.

fallback_url.description: Where an unmatched-but-well-formed slug goes. Absent or null means 404.

base_path_redirect.description: Where a bare GET / on this host goes. Absent falls back to fallback_url.

invalid_short_url_redirect.description: Where a malformed (not just unknown) slug goes. Absent falls back to fallback_url.

DomainPatch.description: `host` is immutable and is not accepted.

short_url.description: The full URL, assembled from the domain host and the slug.

forward_query.description: Merge the incoming query string over the destination's own. Also gates preset_params: off, neither the incoming query nor the preset params touch the destination.

rule_count.description: How many rules (alternate destinations) this link carries.

preset_params.description: Set on the destination at redirect time, overriding both the destination's own query and anything forwarded. Applied only when forward_query is true.

owner_id.description: Null when the key that owned this link was revoked — a link outlives the key that created it.

expires_at.description: Past this, the link resolves like an unknown slug. Null never expires.

listed.description: Opt-in: appears in the domain's public /llms.txt catalogue. See docs/adr/0013.

slug.description: Omit for a generated slug. Reserved words (`api`, `home`, `health`, `robots.txt`, `favicon.ico`, `llms.txt`) are rejected.

preset_params.description: Set on the destination at redirect time, overriding both the destination's own query and anything forwarded. Applied only when forward_query is true.

expires_at.description: Absent or null means the link never expires.

listed.description: Opt-in: appears in the domain's public /llms.txt catalogue. See docs/adr/0013.

rules.description: Ordered alternate destinations, created together with the link.

LinkPatch.description: Strict: `slug` and `domain_id` are immutable, and sending either is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field.

preset_params.description: Set on the destination at redirect time, overriding both the destination's own query and anything forwarded. Applied only when forward_query is true. Send {} to clear.

owner_id.description: Transferring ownership. Your own link, or any link as an admin. 409 if the target key is a viewer — a viewer may not own a link.

expires_at.description: Absent leaves it unchanged; null clears it.

listed.description: Opt-in: appears in the domain's public /llms.txt catalogue. See docs/adr/0013.

rules.description: Replaces the whole ordered set, same as PUT /links/{id}/rules. Absent leaves the existing rules unchanged; send [] to clear them.

Condition.description: One predicate inside a rule. All of a rule's conditions must hold for it to win.

value.description: Absent means "the parameter is present with any value", including an empty one.

conditions.description: ANDed. A rule with no conditions is rejected on write, since it would otherwise match everything.

position.description: Server-owned. The lowest matching position wins.

QrCode.description: A styled QR code for a link's short URL. The encoded data is never stored — it is always the link's current short_url, resolved at read time.

link_name.description: Denormalised from the link, so a list row renders without a second request.

link_owner_id.description: The link's owner, not the QR code's own — a QR code has no owner of its own. A UI courtesy only; the server never trusts this field.

link_id.description: Required — a QR code is never free-floating.

QrCodePatch.description: Strict: `link_id` is immutable — re-pointing a QR code at a different link would invalidate every printed copy — and sending it is a 400 rather than a silently ignored field.

link_id.description: Null is an orphan visit — unknown slug, archived link, or the root path.

slug_requested.description: What the caller asked for, empty for the root path.

is_bot.description: Decided once at ingest. A request with no user agent at all counts as a bot.

os.description: Open vocabulary (unlike platform), lowercased. Null when it couldn't be determined.

browser.description: Open vocabulary (unlike platform), lowercased. Null when it couldn't be determined.

destination.description: The URL actually chosen, after rules and query merging.

query.description: The incoming query as sent, before any merging.

key.description: The bucket's value — a `YYYY-MM-DD` date when grouping by day, otherwise the dimension's value. An empty string means the dimension was never recorded for those visits.

expires_at.description: Absent or null means the key never expires.

ApiKey.description: An API key: the principal. Revoking one is a real delete, and leaves any link it owned unowned.

name.description: Who or what the key is for. Not unique.

prefix.description: The first characters of the secret, so a key is recognisable in a list.

secret.description: The plaintext key, returned exactly once. Only its sha256 is stored, so it cannot be recovered.

ApiKeySummary.description:
What every role below admin sees about another key. `role` lets the
Client UI filter transfer targets with the same rule the server
enforces, rather than offering one it will refuse.

KeyPatch.description: Changing the role of, or revoking, the key you are calling with is a 403: it is the one-way door out of admin.
